decision: Bind Qubes resource calibration to the deterministic orchestration benchmark schedule and send bounded per-worker schedules through a dedicated qrexec workload service.

reviews.correctness: Preferred deriving worker schedules from benchmarkOrchestrationFleet so calibration measures the same DAG/topology used for latency readiness instead of an unrelated idle or generic load.
reviews.security_robustness: Preferred explicit run/workload/topology binding, safe Qube/service names, bounded qrexec timeouts, and stop-all semantics. The workload remains synthetic and must be policy-restricted; no financial or external side effects are introduced.
reviews.latency_resources_regression: Preferred an offline plan plus existing qrexec boundaries. It adds no coordinator/MissionQueue mutations and only start/stop control calls around calibration. A telemetry daemon or privileged dom0 sampler would add lifecycle, credential, and regression surface.

alternatives_rejected: Idle-only resource sampling: cheap but systematically underestimates active worker RAM/CPU.
Generic constant CPU burn: measurable but not representative of the orchestration DAG or topology contention.
Persistent telemetry/workload daemon: higher fidelity potential but materially larger attack, lifecycle, and resource surface before Qubes qualification is green.
qa: Plan must be generated from the same constrained fleet benchmark.
Every mission must map to a capability-compatible worker.
Start/stop hooks must bind runId, workloadId, topology and use bounded qrexec calls.
Malformed service responses and topology/workload mismatches fail closed.
lesson: Resource evidence is useful only when the measured load is causally tied to the workload whose topology is being qualified.
